text:
emma_support: FYI customer acme-prod reporting spike of 502/503s on hosted inference endpoints (/v1/generate) since ~2026-03-17T12:04Z. Customer saw ~30% failed requests, says tokens charged but responses 5xx. Request ids: rI:abc123, rI:def456.

sre_oncall: Looking. Can you paste a raw example request/response and a request-id?

emma_support: Pasted one: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-request-id: rI:abc123
content-type: application/json
{"error":"control-plane dependency failed", "details":"auth/session service timeout"}

eng_runtime: Thanks. I see identical 504s in control-plane logs around those timestamps — routing-policy svc returning 504 to controlplane, and controlplane returning 502 to gateway.

dev_infra: Pulling logs from config-db and auth cluster now. Early note: high tail latencies on configdb connections, connection wait times spike to >8s, many pooled connections in WAIT.

eng_runtime: Relevant log excerpt:
```
2026-03-17T12:03:58Z controlplane routing: request_id=rI:abc123 route_eval_time=235ms upstream_call=authz timeout=10000ms error=upstream_timeout
2026-03-17T12:03:59Z auth-session: request_id=rI:abc123 db_query_time=10050ms status=timeout

```

product_ops: Customer impact: 3 paying tenants; two reported 30% failure rate, one reported intermittent 500s only on long prompts. Priority P1.

emma_support: Customer wants repro steps and ETA. Any mitigation we can advise?

sre_oncall: Short-term mitigation: enable control-plane fallback routing to model-variant L (less stateful) and increase auth-session cache TTL for hosted tier. I'm going to run a routing policy hotfix to fallback after 2s of auth latency.

eng_runtime: On it. Pushing a small control-plane config change: routing policy threshold from 2000ms->2000ms (no change) but adding fallback after 2000ms. Also temporarily increase auth cache TTL from 30s->300s for hosted-prod. Will monitor.

dev_infra: Found one connection leak pattern on the config DB proxy; opening a follow-up ticket to rotate proxy and increase pool size. For now adding a short-term DB connection pool bump + shorter retry backoff.

emma_support: Sending customer suggested workaround: 1) retry with exponential backoff up to 2s 2) if critical, switch to dedicated capacity or pin to model-variant L 3) we applied temporary auth-cache bump and routing fallback. They asked for a timeline.

eng_runtime: ETA for rollback to normal: 30m to validate fallback and measure error rate. If errors don't drop, we'll roll an emergency patch to auth-session to add circuit-breaker and bulkhead.

deploy-bot: deploy started: controlplane-config-hotfix @eng_runtime by eng_runtime (deploy id df-8901)

sre_oncall: After hotfix, monitoring: error rate dropped from 28% -> 4% in 10m; tail latencies for auth-session reduced but still high at p99 ~3.2s. We'll keep incident page updated.

product_ops: Created INC-2026-3445 and linked customer case CS-9987. Set expectation: follow-up postmortem within 48h.

emma_support: Customer updated: "Thanks for quick fix — still seeing occasional 500s but much better. Please send root cause and steps."

eng_runtime: Action items: 1) RCA on config-db proxy leak (dev_infra) 2) implement auth-session circuit breaker + cache strategy (eng_runtime) 3) permanent routing fallback policy (dev_infra + eng_runtime) 4) postmortem and customer summary (product_ops + support).

dev_infra: Filed follow-ups: TICKET-4768 (proxy leak), TICKET-4769 (pool sizing), TICKET-4770 (routing policy as config).

emma_support: Closing loop with customer — let them know we applied temporary fixes and have follow-ups open.

sre_oncall: Marking thread resolved for now; will reopen if error rate >5% for next 1h. :white_check_mark:

eng_runtime: Adding note to run a targeted load test against auth-session with long-prompt workload (seq len 2048) to reproduce. Repro curl: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"model":"large-llm","input":"<long prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -D -
```

emma_support: Thanks everyone — updating customer and INC.

product_ops: Postmortem owner: @eng_runtime. ETA for draft: 48h.
